title: Triangulation of the compatible uniform complete category
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $\varpi$ a uniformizer, $I=(\varpi)$, and $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $T$ be a noetherian scheme of finite dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the completed coefficient sheaf $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and the derived category $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The full subcategory $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], defined by derived completeness, uniformly bounded constructible reduction towers with common adic-lisse finite-type local models, and compatible etale-origin witnesses, contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, all integer shifts, and cones of every morphism between its objects. With the inherited shift and the ambient distinguished triangles whose vertices lie in it, it is a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]; its inclusion into $D(T_{\Proet},A)$ is exact. This assertion concerns the compatible uniform tower category, not merely levelwise bounded constructibility or the constant-coefficient category.

proof.text: Use the exact completion data from the actual reflector. For the locus where its natural unit is invertible, transport units through isomorphisms, use the zero objects and coherent shift square, and apply the two-isomorphism lemma to the unit morphism of distinguished triangles. This proves isomorphism closure and triangulation of intrinsic completeness.

Apply the uniform cohomology criterion. Each constant-coefficient reduction is exact: choose the triangulated structure supplied by derived scalar extension and compose with exact coefficient restriction. The intrinsic constructible homology property is triangulated at each level. The parent proves the following family argument: isomorphisms preserve each bound; shifts send [a,b] to [a-m,b-m]; for a distinguished triangle use the common outside-vertex interval [min(a1,a3),max(b1,b3)] and t-structure extension closure, plus middle-vertex constructibility at every level. Zero lies in every level. Thus the uniform profile is isomorphism-closed and triangulated. Retain the direct finite-level site-comparison import required by the unit route; the compatible-origin portion of the criterion uses this comparison.

Rewrite the unchanged three-clause predicate as the intersection of intrinsic completeness and the uniform profile, using the reduction criterion. Apply the Mathlib intersection instances for isomorphism-closed triangulated properties. The full subcategory inherits the ambient distinguished triangles and exact inclusion.
